advances: The construction selects valid nearest-neighbor multipliers for the original one-dimensional program. It preserves the terminal rows of that selection and localizes positive loss, without assuming a sign for the boundary contributions.

proof:
The supporting slopes exist exactly when adjacent differences are nondecreasing. Each interior slope is chosen between its left and right adjacent differences, and an endpoint slope satisfies its available one-sided condition. Telescoping then proves every supporting inequality. Conversely the two inequalities from an interior site to its neighbors imply the second difference is nonnegative. The feasible set is closed and contains a sufficiently large constant height. Its nonnegative coordinates are bounded on each objective sublevel, proving attainment.

For $q>1$ use the differentiable extension $\sum_i[h_i]_+^q$ with the same gradients on the feasible set. At an optimum the finite polyhedral normal-cone condition applied to the obstacle and second-difference inequalities gives the displayed multipliers and complementarity. When $\beta_i>0$, both adjacent differences at $i$ are equal, so the chosen supporting slope makes both corresponding inequalities tight. The outgoing displacement sum for the equal two-sided flows is zero, giving slope stationarity. Height stationarity is $\lambda_i=s_i+\sum_j\mu_{ij}-\sum_j\mu_{ji}$, exactly the displayed equation. Thus these are multipliers for the same original program, including when the heights are nonunique.

For $q>1$, let $Z$ be the zero-height set. A positive outgoing $\beta_i$ at $i\in Z$ forces both neighboring heights to be zero by complementarity and nonnegativity. Thus no flow leaves $Z$. Summing stationarity over $Z$ gives $\sum_{i\in Z}\lambda_i$ equal to minus the flow into $Z$ from its complement, so both vanish. The remaining internal flow is conservative and has zero mean displacement in each row. Expanding $(j-i)^2=j^2-i^2-2i(j-i)$ and summing against the internal flow gives zero, by conservation for the first difference and slope stationarity for the second. Every nonzero-displacement edge in $Z$ therefore has zero weight. The all-zero case has no nontrivial rows. All neighbors of a positive-$\beta$ site remain in the retained set.

On the retained finite set the positive stopping probabilities $s_i/a_i$ have a positive minimum. The geometric series $N=\sum_{k\ge0}T^k$ converges, and $ND$ records all possible terminal positions under the original transition and stopping probabilities. In row-vector notation, stationarity gives $a=\lambda+aT$, so $\lambda N=a$. Thus $\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)ND$ has the original source marginal $\lambda$ and terminal marginal $s$. Its terminal probability rows sum to one. Since $D+T-\mathrm{Id}$ acts on $f$ as $(\beta_j/a_j)\Delta f_j$ at index $j$ with positive $\beta_j$ and as zero elsewhere, multiplication by $N$ gives the signed row identity. Testing it on $f_j=j$ proves the mean.

At a zero-$\beta$ site the chain stops immediately. Starting at a positive-$\beta$ site, transitions can reach every member of its component $J$ and its two adjacent stopping sites, and no others. This proves the asserted positivity of $W$ and the support. Complementarity gives equal successive slopes throughout $[l-1,r+1]\cap\mathbb Z$. The identity $N=\mathrm{Id}+NT$ gives $N_{ij}=\mathbf 1_{\{j=i\}}+W_{i,j-1}+W_{i,j+1}$ on $J$ and at its adjacent sites, taking missing entries to be zero. On $J$ substitute $N_{ij}=(2+s_j/\beta_j)w_j$ and $\theta_j^{(i)}=N_{ij}s_j/a_j$. At the two adjacent sites the stopping probability is one, giving the stated boundary terms.

For the residual application, take positive parts in the exact identity and use nonnegative $W$. If both neighboring strict residuals are nonempty, the Minkowski midpoint of compact stricter-margin cuts is in the middle strict residual. Brunn–Minkowski, valid even for nonempty null cuts, and continuity from below give $\Delta f_j\le0$. If all three residuals are empty then $\Delta f_j=0$. The projection of $C\setminus H$ is an interval by convexity, and its sampled sites are consecutive within $I$. These two exclusions leave only its boundary indices and their adjacent exterior sites as possible positive terms.

statement:
Let $I=\{L,\ldots,R\}$ be a nonempty finite integer interval, let $e_i\ge0$, and let $q\ge1$. Minimize $\sum_{i\in I}h_i^q$ under $h_i\ge e_i$ and $\Delta h_i=h_{i-1}-2h_i+h_{i+1}\ge0$ at every interior index. The minimum is attained. This feasible set is exactly the projection of the constraints $h_j\ge h_i+g_i(j-i)$ for all $i,j\in I$, with one supporting slope $g_i$ at each site and the same obstacles. At each optimum one can select nonnegative multipliers $\lambda_i,\beta_i$ with $\beta_i=0$ at and outside the endpoints such that
$$
\lambda_i=s_i+2\beta_i-\beta_{i-1}-\beta_{i+1},\qquad
\lambda_i(h_i-e_i)=0,\qquad
\beta_i\Delta h_i=0\quad(L<i<R).
$$
Here obstacle complementarity holds at every site, $s_i=q h_i^{q-1}$ for $q>1$, and $s_i=1$ for $q=1$. The corresponding original supporting-slope KKT system has the convexity flows $\mu_{i,i-1}=\mu_{i,i+1}=\beta_i$ at interior sites and all other flows zero. For $q>1$ zero-height nodes have zero $s_i$, $\lambda_i$, and incident flow.

On the retained nodes with $s_i>0$, put $a_i=s_i+2\beta_i$, $T_{i,i\pm1}=\beta_i/a_i$ and all other transition entries zero, $D_{ii}=s_i/a_i$, $N=(\mathrm{Id}-T)^{-1}$ and $W_{ij}=N_{ij}\beta_j/a_j$. The probability row $\theta^{(i)}=(ND)_{i,\cdot}$ has mean $i$ and is the normalized original terminal coupling row when $\lambda_i>0$. For every real array $f$,
$$
\sum_j\theta^{(i)}_j f_j-f_i=\sum_{j:\beta_j>0} W_{ij}\Delta f_j.
$$
If $\beta_i=0$, the row is the point mass at $i$. Otherwise write $J=[l,r]\cap\mathbb Z$ for the positive-$\beta$ component containing $i$. The coefficients $w_j=W_{ij}$ are positive exactly on $J$ and, extended by zero off $J$, satisfy
$$
(2+s_j/\beta_j)w_j-w_{j-1}-w_{j+1}=\mathbf 1_{\{j=i\}}\qquad(j\in J).
$$
The terminal probabilities on $J$ are $(s_j/\beta_j)w_j$, and the only others are $w_l$ at $l-1$ and $w_r$ at $r+1$. The heights $h$ are affine on $[l-1,r+1]\cap\mathbb Z$.

For $f_j=|C_j\setminus H_j|^{1/d}$ from one original closed cap of an actual convex body with one integer coordinate, the positive row loss is at most $\sum_{j\in J} W_{ij}[\Delta f_j]_+$. Positive summands occur only at boundary indices of the interval of nonempty strict residual sets or at adjacent exterior indices. A point mass has zero loss.
title: Nearest-neighbor KKT multipliers and exact stopping rows on an integer interval
